business_problem: Michelin's centralized on-premises platform lacked the openness and flexibility needed for decentralized teams to access data, tools and technologies at scale and build their own analytics use cases.
solution_summary: Michelin turned the Databricks Data + AI Platform into a self-serve citizen data platform so employees and feature teams could mix local and central data, build their own data products and run analytics without being blocked by a centralized on-premises stack. Data from back-office systems, manufacturing sites and supply-chain processes is unified in a lakehouse where Delta Lake keeps continuously updated datasets available for model training and real-time analysis. Databricks SQL gives analysts a common way to query and visualize results, while isolated cloud workspaces let teams experiment safely and share data products back to the wider organization. One early application used machine learning models trained on historic supply-chain data to predict stock levels 15 days ahead and recommend actions that avoid outages. The same platform now supports hundreds of distributed use cases while preserving governance, collaboration and autonomy for Michelin's decentralized teams.
